brand.name: Stratum
brand.tagline: Earth history, one layer at a time

scenes.text: Two hundred and fifty million years of Earth history, on one ruler.
In the Triassic, every continent was joined in one supercontinent, Pangaea, and the first dinosaurs appeared.
In the Jurassic, Pangaea split apart, giant sauropods roamed, and the first birds took off.
The Cretaceous brought flowering plants, and ended with the asteroid impact at Chicxulub.
In the Paleogene, mammals spread into the empty world, including early primates and the ancestors of whales.
The Pleistocene was an age of ice. Twenty thousand years ago, the sea stood about one hundred and twenty metres lower.
Then the ice retreated, the climate settled, and people began to farm.

props.title: From the dinosaurs to the *first* farmers

eras.name: Triassic
points: All continents form one supercontinent, Pangaea
The first dinosaurs appear, about 230 million years ago

eras.name: Jurassic
points: Pangaea breaks up and the Atlantic begins to open
Giant sauropods such as Brachiosaurus roam
Archaeopteryx, one of the first birds, appears

eras.name: Cretaceous
points: Flowering plants spread across the land
The Chicxulub impact ends the non-bird dinosaurs

eras.name: Paleogene
points: Mammals diversify into the empty niches
Early primates and the first whale ancestors evolve

eras.name: Pleistocene
points: Repeated ice ages bury northern continents in ice
20,000 years ago the sea was about 120 m lower

eras.name: Holocene
points: The climate warms and settles after the last ice age
Farming begins in the Fertile Crescent
